findings.highlight: What about the match is decided!?
findings.evidenceJa: 勝敗が決したがどうした
findings.governingReading: Shirou demands to know why a decided outcome should make him retreat.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed and obscures the defiant “so what?” relation.

findings.highlight: EhKotomine…?
findings.evidenceJa: えって、なんで言峰
findings.governingReading: Shirou breaks off in surprise before asking why Kotomine is there.
findings.explanation: The English runs the interjection and name together and drops the question.

findings.highlight: dead on your feet
findings.evidenceJa: 衰弱しきっていた
findings.governingReading: Both Shirou and Rin were completely debilitated and would die without treatment.
findings.explanation: The English uses an idiom usually meaning extreme tiredness, weakening medical collapse.

findings.highlight: There’s nothing wrong with my body
findings.evidenceJa: 体に異状はない
findings.governingReading: Shirou detects no present bodily abnormality after treatment.
findings.explanation: The English overstates a self-check as categorical health, despite the continuing arm condition.

findings.highlight: The energy that was swallowed by Sakura’s shadow has recovered
findings.evidenceJa: ごっそり削ぎ落とされた体力も回復している
findings.governingReading: The large amount of physical strength shaved away by Sakura’s shadow has recovered.
findings.explanation: The English changes physical stamina into generic energy and the cutting image into swallowing.

findings.highlight: It is three in the morning
findings.evidenceJa: 深夜の三時過ぎだ
findings.governingReading: It is after three in the morning.
findings.explanation: The English removes the “past” qualification.

findings.highlight: the chair I was lying on
findings.evidenceJa: 横になっていた長椅子
findings.governingReading: Shirou rises from the long bench on which he had been lying.
findings.explanation: The English changes a chapel bench into a chair.

findings.highlight: You only had your energy taken away
findings.evidenceJa: おまえは体力だけだったが
findings.governingReading: Only Shirou’s physical strength was depleted, in contrast to Rin’s magical energy.
findings.explanation: The English collapses physical stamina into generic energy and weakens the explicit contrast.

findings.highlight: the land of Tohsaka is good for her
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の土はアレによく馴染む
findings.governingReading: The Tohsaka soil is well matched or familiar to Rin.
findings.explanation: The English changes affinity with the land into a vague claim that it is good for her.

findings.highlight: regain consciousness by tomorrow afternoon
findings.evidenceJa: 明日の昼には意識を取り戻す
findings.governingReading: Rin should regain consciousness by noon tomorrow.
findings.explanation: The English changes noon to the broader and later afternoon.

findings.highlight: home to vampires
findings.evidenceJa: 吸血種が寝床にしていた
findings.governingReading: The ley line is associated with the sleeping place of a vampiric being or species.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes this into multiple vampires and generalizes the bed or lair relation.

findings.highlight: if I keep her buried for a day
findings.evidenceJa: 一晩埋めておけば
findings.governingReading: Kotomine jokes that leaving Rin buried overnight should restore her sharp tongue.
findings.explanation: The English changes one night to a full day.

findings.highlight: she will be back to her impudent self
findings.evidenceJa: 減らず口を取り戻す
findings.governingReading: Rin will recover her inexhaustible sharp tongue.
findings.explanation: The English changes a speech trait into her whole impudent personality.

findings.highlight: this is no time to be hesitating
findings.evidenceJa: ここで踏み止まっている場合じゃない
findings.governingReading: This is no time for Shirou to remain standing here instead of moving.
findings.explanation: The English changes physical delay into indecision.

findings.highlight: these people can’t be fought with weapons from my house
findings.evidenceJa: どうにかなる相手じゃない
findings.governingReading: The expected opposition cannot be handled with weapons Shirou could select at home.
findings.explanation: The English adds plural people before the exact gathering is established.

findings.highlight: all my enemies are at my destination
findings.evidenceJa: 全ての駒が揃っている
findings.governingReading: Shirou infers that every piece in the conflict will be assembled at the destination.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the tactical board metaphor with enemies and categorizes every named figure as his enemy.

findings.highlight: the victor of this Holy Grail War is decided
findings.evidenceJa: 既に勝敗は決した
findings.governingReading: Kotomine asks whether the contest’s outcome is already settled.
findings.explanation: The English promotes a settled outcome into an identified victor.

findings.highlight: the crest worm in her body
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の体内の刻印虫
findings.governingReading: The Crest Worm system inside Sakura can place her under Zouken’s control.
findings.explanation: The English again reduces the implanted worms to one worm.

findings.highlight: I stop at the unexpected reply
findings.evidenceJa: あまりの答えに足が止まる
findings.governingReading: Kotomine’s astonishing answer physically stops Shirou’s feet.
findings.explanation: The English omits the embodied reaction.

findings.highlight: my powers should be of assistance
findings.evidenceJa: 私程度でも有り難いはず
findings.governingReading: Kotomine dryly says that even someone of his modest degree ought to be welcome without Rin.
findings.explanation: The English removes his ironic self-reference and substitutes an assertion about his powers.

findings.highlight: I’m happy for any help
findings.evidenceJa: 協力者が増えてくれる分には不服なんてない
findings.governingReading: Shirou has no objection insofar as another collaborator is added.
findings.explanation: The English invents happiness and broadens the bounded claim to any help.

findings.highlight: We can never understand each other
findings.evidenceJa: 最後まで相容れぬ関係だ
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says their positions will remain irreconcilable or mutually incompatible to the end.
findings.explanation: The English narrows fundamental opposition into inability to understand one another.

findings.highlight: simply for mutual benefit
findings.evidenceJa: 単純な利害の一致
findings.governingReading: Kotomine describes a simple coincidence or alignment of interests.
findings.explanation: The English implies reciprocal benefit rather than temporarily convergent interests.

findings.highlight: they defeated all my Servants
findings.evidenceJa: 私のサーヴァントは全てヤツに敗れた
findings.governingReading: All of Kotomine’s Servants were defeated by one referenced opponent.
findings.explanation: The English changes the unresolved singular opponent into plural “they.”
